🚨 NO DOCTOR IN THE ICU

A 26-year-old dental student walked into a Connecticut ER with pancreatitis and vomiting. Hours later he was dead.

His family's lawsuit says he was moved into a "tele-ICU" at Bridgeport Hospital's Milford Campus, which is owned by Yale New Haven Health. The doctor running the unit was on a TV screen 12 MILES AWAY.

His father says no physician saw his son in person during his ENTIRE four hours in that ICU.

According to the state's own investigation, when an on-site doctor was finally called to intubate him, the doctor got LOST on the way to the ICU.

The lawsuit says he was declared dead by a provider on a video screen.

His family says nobody told them there was no ICU doctor in the building.

This is what happens when hospitals treat intensive care like a cost to cut. 

Fewer doctors on the floor and more screens on the wall.

If you or your parents end up in an ICU, ask one question first: is there a doctor physically in this building?

This family had to learn that the hardest way possible.

posts.text:
Okay I'm sorry but we need to stop acting like this is even a question.

Book Peeta was NOT more gentle than movie Peeta. He was MORE. More everything.

Movie Peeta is just soft. He sits there, he looks sad, he says "stay with me" and everyone cries. That's it.

Book Peeta? Book Peeta had a MOUTH on him. He was funny. He was cocky. He was flirting with Katniss on live TV while she was trying to kill him in her head. "You here to finish me off, sweetheart?" "Remember, we're madly in love." WHO says that in a death game? Peeta does. Because he was never just the nice boy. He was smart, strategic, brave.

And don't get me started on Josh Hutcherson. Was he the perfect Peeta? YES. And he was WASTED. They cut his best scenes, cut his leg, cut his whole personality and then people say "Peeta is boring" or "Katniss should've picked Gale." OF COURSE you think that if you only watched the movies!

Read the books and tell me Peeta is just gentle. He survived hijacking. He survived torture. He survived being turned into a weapon against the girl he loves and he STILL chose to be kind. That's not just gentle, that's strength. That's the whole point of his character.

And let's be real about Gale. In the movies, Gale looks strong and Peeta looks like the soft backup. In the books it's the opposite. Gale is cold and willing to kill innocents. Peeta is the one who sits with Katniss in her nightmares, plants primroses, makes her bread, asks "real or not real" until she feels safe. That's not weak. That's real love.

So no, movie Peeta and book Peeta are NOT the same person. Josh could have BEEN book Peeta easily. Give him the real lines, the humor, the pain, and he would have ended this debate in one scene. But they played it safe.

Book Peeta isn't just gentle. He's gentle AND funny AND strong. If you still think he's boring, you didn't read the books.

The movies made him look like he needed saving, but in the books he was saving Katniss emotionally every single day without asking for anything back.

And honestly, that's why Katniss chose him in the end. Not because he was safe, but because he was the only one who truly saw her.
